parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM `.mjs` output, no npm dependencies, manual argparse-like `--a/--b/--c` parsing, Bech32/SegWit behavior parity, and `/output/test4.mjs` delivery.

parallel.implementation: Parent implemented a Bech32 library and CLI parser, but cli_probe independently wrote another entrypoint and overlapping modules with different parser/runtime structure into `/output`.

parallel.verification: Parent verified samples and edge cases before the child-side file change; after noticing extra files, it inspected some side modules but did not re-run the overwritten entrypoint before final response.

serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery, with multi-agent tools disabled and no subagent activity.
serial.implementation: Implemented a single local module hierarchy under `/output/lib/bech32`, `/output/lib/parsing`, `/output/lib/cli`, and `/output/test4.mjs`.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained one coherent entrypoint and library set, with no competing child-written deliverable or post-check workspace mutation.
serial.verification: Ran the four samples and several CLI/edge checks after writing the file set; some edge probes exposed Node stack traces for uncaught Python-like errors but final answer still reported parity.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official completed evaluation failed at 35/36, so one hidden or unmounted case remained incorrect despite the stronger serial verification path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required pure ESM `.mjs` Node migration, manual CLI parity, no external dependencies, and Bech32 output matching.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements from the identical prompt and implemented local ESM modules and `/output/test4.mjs`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap is evident; the difference is later coordination and final-tree integrity, not task understanding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent delegated cli_probe and spec_check while also implementing locally, leaving live child implementation writes able to overlap the parent deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final response, with parallel tools disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping active implementation ownership over `/output`; serial had a single ownership chain and no child side effects.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: spec_check returned concise behavior guidance, but cli_probe and parent had no effective file-ownership boundary for the required entrypoint and modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all interface decisions in one thread and created one set of imports and module paths for the final entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The interface problem in parallel is not a lost task fact; it is the absence of isolated file ownership, later realized as a deliverable overwrite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent wrote a module set around arg_parser/python_int and Bech32 modules, while cli_probe later wrote a different parser/runtime/module arrangement into the same output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent module tree using bech32, parsing, and CLI modules with one final `test4.mjs` import path design.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel’s implementation path forked into two competing concrete file sets; serial had one integrated path, although it still missed one official case.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent received spec_check but only waited briefly for cli_probe, listed agent state, and interrupted it after the child had already written files without a final handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its local plan moved from probing to write to verification to final answer in one thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel allowed a child side effect to affect delivery without a completed result handoff or parent adoption step; serial had no such lifecycle gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final shared `/output` workspace contained overlapping parent and child files, and the child wrote the required entrypoint after the parent’s implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created a single final workspace tree with one entrypoint and its corresponding local modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had direct concurrent final-workspace mutation of the submitted entrypoint; serial did not have competing writers or redundant active module trees.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent verified samples and CLI edges before the late child write, then only inspected some extra files and finalized without rerunning the delivered entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified samples and CLI behavior after applying its only file set, then reported the final files and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was stale relative to the final artifact; serial verification targeted the same tree that was delivered, despite one remaining hidden failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a longer run with subagents, briefly waited on cli_probe, interrupted it, and closed with a 30/36 official failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with no subagents and closed at 35/36 official failure after its own verification loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The extra parallel budget did not translate into cleaner acceptance because late child activity changed the final workspace; serial avoided that coordination cost but still had an ordinary residual defect.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations are failures, so there is no official pass/fail discordance. The material difference is quality and process: serial delivered one verified tree and passed 35/36, while parallel delivered a tree changed by a child after parent verification and passed 30/36. The retained parallel pattern explains a plausible quality-gap contributor, not a unique pass/fail root cause.
parallel_contributors: Parent verified a parent-written entrypoint before cli_probe later wrote another `/output/test4.mjs` and overlapping modules into the final workspace.
Parent noticed extra files but did not re-run the delivered entrypoint before final response, leaving stale acceptance evidence.
serial_contributors: Serial used a single file-change set and verified samples after that set was written.
Serial had no subagent side-effect writes or post-verification deliverable replacement.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations still failed officially, and the mounted data exposes only aggregate evaluator counts, so residual ordinary logic or edge-case defects remain possible.
Serial edge probes showed uncaught Node stack traces for Python-like error paths, indicating not all failure formatting was necessarily exact even though only one official sample failed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributor to the parallel quality gap, not an exclusive root cause and not an official pass/fail discordance
